entities.name: value, sender or parameter storing part

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation IS an operation that reads the top element of a message-based or procedure-based incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The check operation allows reading the top element of a message-based or procedure-based incoming port queue.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `check` ["(" (PortReceiveOp | PortGetCallOp | PortGetReplyOp | PortCatchOp) | ([`from` Address] ["->" [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]]) ")"].
requirements.original:
[ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." check
  [ "(" 
     ( PortReceiveOp | PortGetCallOp | PortGetReplyOp | PortCatchOp ) |
     ( [ from Address ] 
     [ "->" [ sender ValueRef] 
         [ @index value ValueRef] ] )
   ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `check` operation IS an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original:
NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._ [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." check
  [ "(" 
     ( PortReceiveOp | PortGetCallOp | PortGetReplyOp | PortCatchOp ) |
     ( [ from Address ] 
     [ "->" [ sender ValueRef] 
         [ @index value ValueRef] ] )
   ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation IS a generic operation that gives read access to the top element of a message-based or procedure-based incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The check operation is a generic operation that allows read access to the top element of message-based and procedure-based incoming port queues without removing the top element from the queue.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation SHALL NOT remove the top element from the incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The check operation is a generic operation that allows read access to the top element of message-based and procedure-based incoming port queues without removing the top element from the queue.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: At a message-based port, the `check` operation SHALL handle values of a certain type.
requirements.original: The check operation has to handle values of a certain type at message-based ports and to distinguish between calls to be accepted, exceptions to be caught and replies from previous calls at procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: At a procedure-based port, the `check` operation SHALL distinguish between calls to be accepted, exceptions to be caught and replies from previous calls.
requirements.original: The check operation has to handle values of a certain type at message-based ports and to distinguish between calls to be accepted, exceptions to be caught and replies from previous calls at procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation uses the receiving operations `receive`, `getcall`, `getreply` and `catch`, together with their matching and value, sender or parameter storing parts, to define the conditions to be checked and the information to be optionally extracted.
requirements.original: The receiving operations receive, getcall, getreply and catch together with their matching and value, sender or parameter storing parts, are used by the check operation to define the conditions that have to be checked and the information to be optionally extracted.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation SHALL check only the top element of an incoming port queue.
requirements.original: It is the top element of an incoming port queue that shall be checked (it is not possible to look into the queue).

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation CANNOT look into the incoming port queue beyond the top element.
requirements.original: It is the top element of an incoming port queue that shall be checked (it is not possible to look into the queue).

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: If the incoming port queue is empty, the `check` operation fails.
requirements.original: If the queue is empty the check operation fails.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: If the incoming port queue is not empty, the `check` operation takes a copy of the top element and performs the specified receiving operation on the copy.
requirements.original: If the queue is not empty, a copy of the top element is taken and the receiving operation specified in the check operation is performed on the copy.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: If the receiving operation fails, i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled, the `check` operation fails.
requirements.original: The check operation fails if the receiving operation fails i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation fails, the copy of the top element of the incoming port queue IS discarded.
requirements.original: In this case the copy of the top element of the queue is discarded and test execution continues in the normal manner, i.e. the statement or alternative next to the check operation is evaluated. The check operation fails if the receiving operation fails i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation fails, test execution continues in the normal manner by evaluating the statement or alternative next to the `check` operation.
requirements.original: In this case the copy of the top element of the queue is discarded and test execution continues in the normal manner, i.e. the statement or alternative next to the check operation is evaluated. The check operation fails if the receiving operation fails i.e. the matching criteria are not fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: If the receiving operation is successful, the `check` operation is successful.
requirements.original: The check operation is successful if the receiving operation is successful.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation is successful, the value, sender or parameter storing parts of the receiving operation, if any, are executed, storing the message or a part of it, the sender's address or component reference, the parameters of the call or reply or the value of the exception in the associated variables.
requirements.original: In this case, the value, sender or parameter storing parts of the receiving operation, if any, are executed, i.e. the message and/or a part of it, the sender's address or component reference, the parameter(s) of the call or reply or the value of the exception are stored in the associated variables. The check operation is successful if the receiving operation is successful.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.condition: check is used as a stand-alone statement
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone `check` statement IS a shorthand for an `alt` statement with the `check` operation as the only alternative.
requirements.original: If check is used as a stand-alone statement, it is considered to be a shorthand for an alt statement with the check operation as the only alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: In the case of one-to-many connections, the `check` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: In the case of one-to-many connections the check operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner. **Check from a specific sender**

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A restriction of the `check` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted by the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection IS a simple case of a one-to-many connection, so the `from` clause MAY also be used with a `check` operation on a one-to-one connection.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:check-any-operation
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation with no argument list checks whether anything waits for processing in an incoming port queue.
requirements.original: A check operation with no argument list allows checking whether something waits for processing in an incoming port queue. **Check any operation**

requirements.subject: ent:check-any-operation
requirements.canonical: The check any operation MAY use a `from` clause to distinguish between different senders in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.original: The check any operation allows to distinguish between different senders (in case of one-to-many connections) by using a from clause and to retrieve the sender by using a shorthand assignment part with a sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:check-any-operation
requirements.canonical: The check any operation MAY retrieve the sender by a shorthand assignment part with a `sender` clause.
requirements.original: The check any operation allows to distinguish between different senders (in case of one-to-many connections) by using a from clause and to retrieve the sender by using a shorthand assignment part with a sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on any port IS denoted by the `any port` keywords.
requirements.original: To check on any port, use the any port keywords. **Check on any port**

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on any port of a specific port array IS denoted by the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
requirements.original: To check on any port from a specific port array, indices use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier. **Check on any port from a port array**

ambiguity.issue: The phrase 'from a specific port array, indices use' is garbled; the word 'indices' appears to be an editorial leftover.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` PortArrayRef construct of a `check` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To check on any port from a specific port array, indices use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on a single-dimensional port array MAY store the index of the port at which the operation was successful in a variable of type `integer`.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: A `check` operation on a multi-dimensional port array MAY store the index of the successful port in an integer array or `record of integer` variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: When a `check` operation checks a port array for a matching message, call, reply or exception, the `check` operation iterates the port indices from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for a matching message, call, reply or exception, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the `check` operation iterates over the ports from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

readings: The `check` operation iterates such that the last (rightmost) index varies fastest, i.e. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The `check` operation iterates such that the first (leftmost) index varies fastest, i.e. [0][0], [1][0], [0][1], [1][1].
ambiguity.issue: 'From innermost to outermost dimension' can be read either way; the given example sequence fixes the rightmost-index-fastest order, which is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all criteria makes the `check` operation successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Using the `check` operation in a wrong manner, e.g. checking for an exception at a message-based port, SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: a) Using the check operation in a wrong manner, e.g. check for an exception at a message-based port shall cause a test case error.

readings: Any misuse of the `check` operation (e.g. a `catch` on a message-based port) SHALL cause a runtime test case error.
Misuse of the `check` operation that can be detected statically SHALL be rejected at compile time; only remaining misuse SHALL cause a test case error.
ambiguity.issue: 'Wrong manner' is only illustrated by one example, and NOTE 3 says most misuse can be detected statically; the literal reading (test case error) is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `check` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `check` operation.
requirements.original: b) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the check operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `check` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `check` operation.
requirements.original: b) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the check operation.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `check` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in a `check` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: c) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection (`@index`) in a `check` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: d) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the port array.
requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the port array.
requirements.original: f) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

ambiguity.issue: 'The same as the dimension of the respective port array' means the number of dimensions of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.original: f) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `sender` or `@index` clause of a `check` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable IS the result produced by the `check` operation, and later evaluation of the variable does not invoke the `check` operation again.
requirements.original: g) If a variable referenced in the sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the check operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the check operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: both from and sender clause are present
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the template in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: h) If the check operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: sender clause present, no from clause
requirements.canonical: If the `check` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.

readings: The type of the actual sender (address or component reference determined at runtime) SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.

The address type associated with the port (address type bound to the port type, or the component type) SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause, checked statically.
ambiguity.issue: 'The sender' is not specified as a value or a type; NOTE 4 suggests a check whenever the sender type can be determined, so the first reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference in a `check` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: i) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `check` statements.
requirements.original: j) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone check statements.

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The correct usage of the `check` operation CAN in most cases be checked statically, before or during compilation.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: In most cases the correct usage of the check operation can be checked statically, i.e. before/during compilation.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: An error due to a type mismatch IS possible if the types in the receive part of a `check` operation are not compatible with the types in the assignment part.
requirements.original: NOTE 4: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: If the `from` clause is missing and the type of the sender can be determined but is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause, an error due to a type mismatch IS possible.
requirements.original: NOTE 4: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.
